subject: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R

messages.author: 6bc824f1fe8a19fe
messages.subject: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R
parts:
Hello Filipe and all FieldImageR users, this amazing R package!

First of all, thank you for all the work you put into this.

I'm working with a lighter version (77 mb) of a larger file with 1 Gb to import in R.
After importing the file, I'm using the raster::aggregate function, as recommended, to reduce the size and make possible the processing.

Original image dim:
> dim(EX1)
[1] 29500 30789     3

Codes I'm using to resize the image:
X1.lite <- aggregate(EX1, fact=50, fun=max))
or
X1.lite <- aggregate(EX1, fact=50, fun=mean))

After resize, image dim:
> dim(EX1.lite)
[1] 590 616   3

I'd appreciate if I have some thoughts on two situations:

1) The original orthomosaic has 4 experimental fields that I need to analyse separately.
If I have to resize the whole orthomosaic (using raster::aggregate), I think I'm losing information. It is even hard to identify and select the 4 corners of the experiment for the function fieldCrop. I can barely see where the experiments are in the picture. To perform the experiments in the field, I placed identification markers on each corner of each experiment. In the orthomosaic they are very clear to identify, but I can't see them in the R screen.

(In this example, the image is too bright because I used "fun=max" in the raster::aggregate)

2) After cropping the image, I use the functions to rotate the image
EX1.Rotated<-fieldRotate(mosaic = EX1.Crop,theta = 40.101)

But when I want to plot the rotated Image:

With the image before the fieldRotate, I have min and max values in a range of 0 to 255. After the fieldRotate, the range changes:



So, 1) what is your approach to first generate and/or to slice a specific and smaller orthomosaic for each experiment, prior to using the raster::aggregate function? Is it possible to do it in R?
Note: I also tried to use the fieldCrop function without resizing with raster::aggregate but the processing time is impracticable.
2) Am I using the raster::aggregate function the correct way? Might it be the cause of the fieldRotate errors?

Best Regards,

--
Danilo

messages.author: 43fff63c72626b1b
messages.subject: Re: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R
parts:
Dear Danilo,

If you have access to the images used to generate the orthomosaic, then I will suggest you redo the mapping using WebODM. It gives a much smaller orthomosaic file which will run easily on any standard computer in R.

Cheers,
Kassim.

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: Orthomosaic size reduction or orthomosaic preparation prior to import in R
parts:
Hi Danilo,

Thank you for asking and thank you for your msg... I really appreciate it.

My apologies for my delay to answering. I was harvesting these last two weeks. 

Well, let’s see. For the first question I believe there are some possibilities. You are doing right using the function aggregate. However, try to use fact=4, 6 or 8. This function is going to average pixels inside the plots (reducing the resolution, supper great strategy). Then, you can use the parameter fastPlot=T on fieldCrop function. Probably, it will take some time to run, because R was not made for huge data/images. But I believe on this way you will get better results. 

Another possibility is to make a mosaic with lower resolution with WebODM as suggested by Kassim. Thank you kassim for helping…!!!

The second question. I don’t know yet why it happens. Actually, it is the first time that I saw this output. I developed one function for plotting RGB images when they do not follow the 0-250 restriction. Please, try to use the code:

 plotRGB(RGB.rescale(EX1.Rotated, num.band = 3))

 Please, let me know if it works for you ...!!!

All the best,

Filipe
